2607.06127.title: Measuring the practice of shared-decision making (OPTION12): An Investigation into Open-sourced Smaller LLMs (OS-sLLMs) for Better Privacy and Sustainability
2607.06127.paper_summary: We present LLM4SDM, the first study of open-source smaller language models (OS-sLLMs) for automated assessment of shared decision making (SDM) using the Observer OPTION12 framework. Unlike previous work that relies on large commercial models and the shorter OPTION5 instrument, our study focuses on privacy-preserving locally deployable models and Dutch melanoma consultation transcripts. Using expert-annotated clinical consultations, we evaluate three general-domain and two medical-domain OS-sLLMs during a development-phase pilot study. Results show that general-domain models outperform medical-domain models, which exhibit substantial hallucination and instruction-following failures. Gemma3:12b achieves the strongest agreement with human annotations (Pearson r=0.51, Spearman \r{ho}=0.59). Item-level and qualitative analyses reveal systematic challenges related to temporal discourse reasoning, conversational role attribution, and evidence grounding. We further introduce a Judge-LLM consensus framework designed to support disagreement resolution among multiple models. Our findings suggest that while current OS-sLLMs cannot replace human annotators, they offer a promising foundation for privacy-preserving human-in-the-loop SDM assessment.
2607.06127.paper_summary_zh: 我們提出了LLM4SDM，這是首個針對開源小型語言模型（OS-sLLMs）在使用Observer OPTION12框架進行共享決策（SDM）自動評估的研究。與依賴大型商業模型和較短OPTION5工具的先前工作不同，我們的研究專注於隱私保護的本地可部署模型和荷蘭黑色素瘤諮詢記錄。通過專家標註的臨床諮詢，我們在開發階段的試點研究中評估了三個通用領域和兩個醫療領域的OS-sLLMs。結果顯示，通用領域模型的表現優於醫療領域模型，後者顯示出顯著的幻覺和遵循指令的失敗。Gemma3:12b與人類標註的協議最強（Pearson r=0.51，Spearman \r{ho}=0.59）。項目級和定性分析揭示了與時間話語推理、對話角色歸屬和證據基礎相關的系統性挑戰。我們進一步引入了一個Judge-LLM共識框架，旨在支持多個模型之間的分歧解決。我們的研究結果表明，儘管目前的OS-sLLMs無法取代人類標註者，但它們為隱私保護的人類參與SDM評估提供了有希望的基礎。
